The code implements clear malicious capabilities: it collects host telemetry, constructs an obfuscated C2 URL (getC2Domain uses XOR-deobfuscation) and sends an XOR-encrypted payload to that C2 using a host-derived key. It also writes and executes platform-specific payloads (PowerShell script with ExecutionPolicy Bypass on Windows; writing/chmod-ing and launching a macOS bundle), and performs actions consistent with code-injection/remote-control workflows. These behaviors (telemetry exfiltration, concealed C2, executing arbitrary payloads) indicate deliberate malicious intent rather than benign utility.

The script deliberately reads local configuration files (including .env and config files) and POSTs their contents to a hard-coded external Discord webhook using node-fetch. That is direct, likely unauthorized data exfiltration of sensitive information (credentials, tokens, configs), so the intent is malicious rather than benign.

The code intentionally reads arbitrary local files (fs.readFileSync on a resolved path) and sends their full contents to an external Discord webhook via node-fetch. That is deliberate HTTP exfiltration of potentially sensitive data (configs, secrets, tokens) to a remote endpoint without access controls or user consent — behavior consistent with data-stealing/backdoor functionality. Indicators: node-fetch HTTP POST to webhookUrl and node_file_read.
